messages.subject: Decimal estimates
parts:
Dear Distance-samplers,

I am getting estimates of Density in decimals instead of integer numbers, but usually density and abundance are counts and statistically analyzed as such.

I cannot find a way to tell Distance to calculate my estimates in integers, and rounding the estimates does not seem a very elegant approach. Has anyone an idea about how to do this?

Many thanks in advance.
Best regards,
Ana María.

--
Ana María Prieto Ramírez
PhD student
Departement of Conservation Biology
Center for Environmental Research UFZ, Leipzig
Zoologisches Forschungsmuseum Alexander Koenig
University of Bonn

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Decimal estimates
parts:
Ana Maria

Density estimates most certainly can take on decimal values.  If there are 100 animals inhabiting a woodland 33ha in size, the density would be 33.333 animals per hectare.  I believe the estimates of abundance produced by the Distance for Windows software are reported in whole numbers.
